approver: Owner ruling 2026-07-28 (prices supplied by the owner)
summary: DEF-010 (pricing half). Makes services_catalog.default_price NULLABLE so 'not yet priced' is representable, and applies the owner's prices to the three services that were sitting at 0.00: LLP accounts production £1000.00, Sole trader accounts £250.00, Trust Registration Service £250.00. One ALTER COLUMN pair and three guarded UPDATEs; no row is added, removed or deactivated.

problem.context: Zero is not a neutral default in this product. A zero unit price means INCLUDED everywhere — isIncludedLine() in src/lib/quote-defaults.ts drives it, and the value is excluded from the one-off total, the monthly total and the Stripe line-item builders, then printed as 'Included' in the engagement letter.
problem.consequence: Three catalogue services sat at 0.00, so adding one to a proposal committed the practice, in the signed contract, to performing that work free of charge. An accountant had no signal that anything was wrong: the line looked deliberate.
problem.ruling: Owner, 2026-07-28: do not invent default prices; make unpriced a real state; and price these three. The prices below are the owner's.
problem.deliberately_not_done: Other services at 0.00 are left alone. Zero is legitimate where a service really is included at no charge, and only these three were identified as unpriced. Rewriting every zero would silently change the commercial meaning of services nobody reviewed.

expected_objects.object: services_catalog.default_price is nullable with no column default
expected_objects.verify_via: db_schema -> public.services_catalog.default_price is_nullable = YES and column_default is null. This is what makes 'unpriced' expressible; without it every unpriced service must claim to be free.

expected_objects.object: LLP accounts production = 1000.00, Sole trader accounts = 250.00, Trust Registration Service = 250.00
expected_objects.verify_via: db_select services_catalog where name in those three -> the stated prices, for every organization that carried them at 0.00. A practice that had already priced one must be unchanged (the UPDATEs are guarded on COALESCE(default_price,0) = 0).

expected_objects.object: No catalogue row was deactivated or removed by this migration
expected_objects.verify_via: Compare the count of active services before and after. In particular sa_mtd must remain active — it carries canonical_service_code 'self_assessment_mtd_quarterly' and doubles as the client type, so deactivating it would stop MTD job materialisation. It is hidden from the quote BUILDER in app code, not disabled in data.

rollback.assessment: The price updates are reversible by setting the three back to 0.00 — which reinstates the free-of-charge exposure. Restoring NOT NULL on default_price is only possible once no row holds NULL.
rollback.data_risk: Low. Three guarded UPDATEs on catalogue rows; no quote, line, invoice or job is touched. Existing quote_lines already carry their own unit_price and are unaffected — this changes the DEFAULT offered for future lines, not any agreed price.

Confirm the card returns green AND a row exists in supabase_migrations.schema_migrations (verify against LIVE, not just Test).

post_apply_followups: The send-time guard from the same ruling is NOT in this release: blocking a quote from being sent until every line is priced, explicitly Included, or explicitly No charge requires a line-level treatment field to tell 'Included' apart from 'No charge' — both are £0 on the invoice but say different things in the engagement letter. That is its own increment; this migration makes the unpriced state it depends on expressible, and closes the immediate exposure by pricing the three named services.

The app currently renders a NULL default_price as 'not priced' in the service picker. Any other surface that formats default_price must be checked for the same, or a NULL will render as £0.00 and re-create the confusion this fixes.
